conclusions: The linear problem (1.1) is a conservation law of the form (1.8) with the linear flux f(v) = Av (printed pages 3–4, sentence crossing the page boundary).

Under this flux substitution, q_t(x,t) + ∂_x(f(q(x,t))) = 0 specializes to q_t(x,t) + A q_x(x,t) = 0. This identity of differential expressions explicates the selected assertion; the source does not separately state it as a quantified equivalence theorem (printed page 1, equation (1.1); printed page 3, equation (1.8); printed page 4, opening sentence).
definitions_and_conventions: Subscripts t and x denote partial derivatives (printed page 1, paragraph following equation (1.1)).
f is the flux function, and f′(q) is its Jacobian matrix in the quasilinear expression (printed page 3, equations (1.8)–(1.9) and adjacent text).

Aq denotes matrix multiplication of the constant m × m matrix by the state vector; the zero in the system is the zero vector in R^m, as determined by the stated dimensions (printed page 1, equation (1.1) and explanatory paragraph; printed page 4, f(q) = Aq).
Hyperbolicity of (1.1) means that A has real eigenvalues with m linearly independent corresponding eigenvectors (printed page 3, opening discussion).

The selected assertion refers to the m-component system, not only scalar advection (printed page 1, equation (1.1) and q : R × R → R^m).

The spatial derivative in (1.8) acts on x ↦ f(q(x,t)), with t fixed; it is not merely the flux evaluated at q_x (printed page 3, equation (1.8)).

For f(v) = Av, the Jacobian is A, explaining the agreement of quasilinear form (1.9) with (1.1); this is an analyst derivation from the displayed formulas (printed pages 1, 3, and 4, equations (1.1), (1.9), and the opening linear-flux sentence).

The assertion identifies a PDE as a conservation law with a specified flux; it does not assert existence, uniqueness, initial data, or boundary data (printed pages 3–4, selected sentence and equations (1.1), (1.8)).
The specified flux is exactly linear, f(v) = Av, without an added constant or explicit dependence on x or t (printed page 4, opening sentence).

contract_plain_english: The constant-coefficient real linear system q_t + A q_x = 0 for an m-component field in one space dimension is a conservation law q_t + ∂_x(f(q)) = 0 with flux f(v) = Av (printed page 1, equation (1.1); printed page 3, equation (1.8); printed page 4, opening sentence). Constancy and linearity explain the agreement of the spatial terms. The selected passage states this identification without an exact regularity class; the surrounding source treats smoothness and discontinuous solutions separately (printed page 4, Section 1.1.2).
